newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close shade higher in volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close shade higher in volatile trade.

text.p: Delhi shares closed marginally higher in mixed trade on Thursday as heavy buying by foreign institutional investors (FIIs) offset selling by speculators, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 1.68 points higher at 751.55. The index had slipped to 746.86 at 1.00 p.m. (0730 GMT).

Traders said guarded caution was creeping into a market which had been on a buying spree after Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda promised in late 1996 that the government would soon announce measures to bolster the capital markets.
"The market's behaviour has been confusing and it was difficult to predict any definite trend," said Manoj Choraria of brokers Choraria Investments.
Deve Gowda said in December that he would announce measures to stimulate growth and shore up financial markets before leaving for an economic summit in Switzerland on Friday.
"The clear picture of the market would emerge only after the announcement of much awaited economic package, slated for tomorrow," said another broker.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram was quoted as saying on Thursday that more Indian reforms were on the government's agenda.
"Overall, to boost the economy, some more reforms are on the anvil," Chidambaram told the Press Trust of India (PTI) news agency in an interview.
Traders have warned that the stock markets could fall sharply if the promised measures fell short of market expectations.
"If the package falls short of marketmen's expectations, the market is certain to react sharply," said Ajit Sial of brokers Sial and Company.
Reliance Industries, which rose seven rupees to 277 on heavy buying by FIIs, led the recovery, brokers said.
Larsen and Toubro ended 1.45 rupees higher at 248.
State Bank of India dropped 3.40 rupees to 293 as speculators booked profits.
